vo: Before it copies anything, the Bot needs to know how to watch an ad. That's what a breakdown guide is for.
Mine asks for five things: the hook in the first two seconds, every cut, what's on screen, the exact words, and the call to action.
Attach the guide and write: read this, then break down the full video.
The Bot measures the cuts, writes the script word for word, and lists every scene with its timing.
It even builds a contact sheet, a grid of frames, and saves the whole thing as a file you can reuse.
Look at what it found: the hook isn't the product. It's the tired face. The product only shows up at second four.
It also counts the words. This ad says about seventy words in twenty-three seconds, so your new script has to fit the same length.
Tell it to save this method as a skill. Next time you just say: break this one down, the same way.
Now swap in your product. Upload one clean photo, front-facing, on a plain background.
Then one prompt: recreate this ad with my product, use Seedance 2.5, keep the structure, and rewrite the lines for cold brew.
Before it renders, ask to see the new script. It keeps the same beats: tired at two p.m., found this, here's how it tastes, will you try it?
Change any line you don't like now. Editing a sentence costs nothing; re-rendering a video costs credits and minutes.
Pick the creator and the voice in plain words too: late twenties, friendly, a little sleepy, kitchen in morning light.
The Bot maps the old structure onto your can, rewrites the script, writes the video prompt, and sends it to the model.
A thirty-second clip takes a few minutes. The Bot checks the job and pings you when it's ready.
And here's the result: same rhythm, same hook, new product, new words.
Side by side with the original, the beats line up almost frame for frame.
Before you use it, watch it once yourself. Check the product looks right and every claim is true.
Sometimes a take comes out wrong: an extra finger, a label that melts, a can that changes colour halfway.
Don't start over. Tell the Bot exactly what's wrong and which seconds: at second six the label is blurry, redo only that part.
Next, one ad is a guess. Three ads are a test.
Ask: make three variations of this ad with different creators, and keep the script the same.
Each version speaks to a different viewer: a student before class, a nurse after a night shift, a dad at six a.m.
The Bot renders all three at once and shows them side by side.
You can vary the first line too. Same product, three different hooks.
Everything lands in your Drive folder, named and ready.
